date: 2026-07-01

A course for high school students on the mathematics behind machine learning. Each day combines a lecture, a guided Python walkthrough in a Jupyter notebook, a hands-on activity and short reflection questions. The course ends with a group [project](project.qmd) on a real dataset.

- [Class notes](https://1drv.ms/o/c/f0f4bc0cf8b335c4/IgANTUh7iqV0TZ3ReQjYH6ZRAewfB634Daynp0Da3f1Qvi8?e=PMVm8q) (OneNote, written in class)

## Daily outline

### Day 1: Introduction

- [Neural Network Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org/)
- Introduction to Python

### Day 2: Modeling and descriptive statistics

- Cleaning real datasets (penguins, car fuel economy)
- [Overfitting example](https://apurvanakade.github.io/VisualMath/model-fitting/polynomial-fit/)

### Day 3: Regression

- Predicting penguin body mass and fuel economy
- Activity: plot and minimize the $L^1$ error of a line through data

### Day 4: Supervised learning and classification

- Classifying penguin species and car origin
- [Google's Teachable Machine](https://teachablemachine.withgoogle.com/train/)
- [ML Playground](https://www.ccom.ucsd.edu/~cdeotte/programs/classify.html)
- Activity: an animal guessing game

### Day 5: Multiple linear regression and dimension reduction

- [How to use t-SNE effectively](https://distill.pub/2016/misread-tsne/)
- [Visualizing MNIST](https://colah.github.io/posts/2014-10-Visualizing-MNIST/)

### Day 6: Neural networks

- [Neural Network Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org/)
- Activity: a mystery network worksheet

### Day 7: Convolutional neural networks

- [CNN visualization](https://adamharley.com/nn_vis/)
- Activity: mystery filters and a worked example of a convolution

### Day 8: Using pre-trained models

- Using a pre-trained model from Hugging Face
